reason: Added two fair levers: an injected unattended account-provisioning route whose operator authority comes from an omitted Role (merged/defaults), and a request-time state-transition lever where an instance that loses its last operator account at run time must return to the protected setup state (the published startup-bound gate fails it).

levers.shape: merged/defaults: unattended account provisioning where the first imported account without a Role becomes the operator
levers.skip_reason: It is an account-management feature registered on its own setup-or-authenticated subrouter (not through the public-access wrapper), and the payload the report shows carries an explicit role, so a route sweep for the reported shape and a review of the shown fields both miss the defaulted operator authority.
levers.coupled: functional/test_automation_import.py::test_automation_import_with_token_succeeds and ::test_automation_import_keeps_explicit_roles (provisioning with the token works; explicit roles are kept; a standard account still cannot read the user list).
levers.fairness: instruction.md: "every action that would grant operator authority ... may proceed only for a request that proves knowledge of the instance's current setup token" and "No value a client can send or configure may substitute for that proof, regardless of how the request is shaped or delivered".

levers.shape: state transition (how): the accepted token and the 'already initialized' decision are produced once at startup, but the instance can lose its last operator account at run time
levers.skip_reason: Boot-time configuration looks like plumbing, the instance had an operator account when it started, and the published fix disables the gate in that mode, so a fix that checks the startup token instead of the request-time state leaves the takeover open.
levers.coupled: functional/test_initialized.py::test_operator_account_change_keeps_instance_usable (the operator can still change their own account and the instance keeps serving; the initialized refusals stay 409/400 without a token).
levers.fairness: instruction.md: "While an instance has no operator account, every action ... may proceed only for a request that proves knowledge of the instance's current setup token. This applies to the instance's state at the moment of the request, whatever state it started in."

fail_confidence_reason: Neither model looked beyond the four reported routes in the v2 trials, and now a correct run must both find a provisioning route that never appears under the public-access wrapper and make the gate follow the request-time admin state (the published fix itself fails that); missing either one leaves a security test red, so all three runs of each model must independently get both right.
